title: the proportion line (the proportion as relation, the fraction as its value, one division in two languages; 0:0 the evenness, declared, never valued)

lesson.statement: a proportion is a relation between two parts of my line: the part held to the part compared — declared for every pair of parts, scaled alike without changing the relation, and named by its reduced form; zero to zero is the evenness of the two empty parts — i have nothing and they have nothing, so we are even on this — declared, never valued; at the line end eighty-four

a fraction is the VALUE of a proportion: its denominator must be a positive part of the line, and its value is the division read in two languages at once — the whole parts (the quotient) and the part left over (the remainder carried over the denominator), so five over three is one and two thirds, and five mod three is two, one division in either word; zero over zero holds no value on my line, because the part you count with is zero parts; at the line end eighty-four

theorems.statement: the proportion line of my store is filed of record: the relation and its value are two jobs of one division — the proportion is declared for every pair of parts and named by its reduced form, the fraction is valued only over a positive part, and zero to zero is the evenness of the two empty parts, declared, never valued; filed on the line, at the line end eighty-four
